properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-11 on Anthony's word. NO NEW VOCABULARY WAS NEEDED, and finding that out is the whole result.

THE ANSWER: a Decision `OBSOLETES` the thing it withdrew. PUT THE DECISION AT THE SOURCE.

That dissolves the objection this node was opened over. Point (3) above says both retirement edges "presume a successor to sit at the source end. A discontinued thing with no replacement has NOTHING TO PUT THERE. You cannot draw OBSOLETES from nothing." True — but a discontinuation ALWAYS has a decision behind it even when it has no replacement, so the decision is the honest source. `OBSOLETES` is already `* -> *` in schema/inference.yaml and its hint already reads "source makes target redundant or deprecated". So: no edge type, no enum value, NO SCHEMA STAMP MOVE, and no upgrade doc — none of which option (A) or (B) could have claimed.

⭐ AND IT ANSWERS `dec:one-retire-edge`'S REAL QUESTION AS A SIDE EFFECT. That decision asked, since July, what SHOULD consult a retirement edge — "retiring something marks it and changes nothing. A retired capability still counts in every rollup, still raises its gaps, still appears in delivery arithmetic." Four readers now exist, which is four more than either retirement edge has ever had:
  · `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability`, `unverified_capability` fall silent
  · delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier
So OBSOLETES is no longer a marker nothing reads. Whether SUPERSEDES survives at all is still `dec:one-retire-edge`'s to settle, and it is now a smaller question: one of the two words has a job.

⚠️ ONLY AN ACCEPTED DECISION DISCONTINUES ANYTHING. A `proposed` withdrawal has withdrawn nothing; the thing keeps counting until somebody with the authority says so. That is `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` applied to the retire path, and it is pinned by a test that fails if the check is dropped.

⚠️ THE CASCADE IS DELIBERATE. Withdrawing the thing that met a need does not meet the need, so the requirement it served drops back to UNSATISFIED and is asked about again — "covered, deferred, or dropped?". Without that, a discontinuation would be invisible one hop away and the design would keep reporting a need as met by something that no longer exists. Applying this to the content store surfaces exactly that, and the two requirements it served are now open questions for Anthony rather than silent claims.

⚠️ AND THE NUMBERS SAY WHY THEY MOVED. `DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued` counts the skipped edges, because a discontinuation that made delivery fall with no mention is the silent-drop failure this project forbids everywhere else: the count drops, nothing explains it, and a reader concludes the design regressed.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT CLAIMED HERE:
  · `dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state` (Alex's) is NOT closed by this. It covers the ABANDONED case; it says nothing about a WISH NOBODY EVER AGREED TO, which has no decision behind it to be the source of an OBSOLETES edge. That half is still `dec:exploratory-staging`'s.
  · A Verification whose code was deleted still reads `passing`. `ver:content-store` is the live instance. Nothing here fixes that, and marking the verification obsoleted does not change its status field.
  · Nothing reads discontinuation for Components, Interfaces or Artifacts. Only the capability detectors and delivery consult it today, which is stated rather than left to be discovered.
properties.name: DECIDED — a Decision OBSOLETES what it withdrew, and three detectors plus delivery now read it
properties.rationale: Anthony asked on 2026-08-09 for a way to say "we built this and then decided against it". Searching before building found that the vocabulary already held it, in a direction nobody had tried: the objection was that a discontinued thing has no successor for the source end of a retirement edge, and the answer is that the DECISION is the source. That costs nothing — no schema change, no stamp move, no upgrade doc — and it gives OBSOLETES its first reader in the process, which is the question dec:one-retire-edge has been waiting on since July. Shipped WITH its readers deliberately: this project has now found three markers nothing reads (enforced, SUPERSEDES, OBSOLETES itself), and a fourth would have been the defect rather than the fix.
